event.name: Celebrate Little Saigon 2026
event.summary: Celebrate Little Saigon is back on Saturday, August 15th! 🌞🎉
event.description:
Join us for a free, all-ages community festival hosted by Friends of Little Sài Gòn. Enjoy live music, drag bingo, community joy, and food!

Celebrate Little Saigon is a free, all-ages community street festival honoring the food and culture of Seattle’s Vietnamese and Southeast Asian communities. What began in 2011 as a grassroots event with four food vendors and folding chairs has grown into a summer tradition welcoming hundreds of attendees each year.

Held across Hoa Mai Park, Nisei Veterans Hall Parking Lot, and Little Saigon Creative, the festival features local performers and vendors of the Southeast Asian diaspora who have ties to Little Saigon. Enjoy live music, family-friendly activities, and playful programming like the Phở Eating Contest, Drag Bingo, and the FIRST-EVER Spring Roll Wrapping Contest. More than two dozen local vendors will offer food, drinks, handmade goods, and local resources, reflecting the neighborhood’s cultural richness.

Organized by Friends of Little Sài Gòn, Celebrate Little Saigon is more than a festival; it’s a space to honor heritage, support small businesses, and build joy and connection in the heart of Little Saigon.

event.name: Washington 250: Making American History in Seattle
event.summary: Join us to commemorate the first-ever “Day of Remembrance" with Frank Abe and Densho.
event.description:
Connected to the Washington state-wide celebration of America’s 250 anniversary, we have collaborated with Densho on a mini-exhibit for the "Out of Many, One" initiative.

The summertime exhibit features the poster from the first Japanese American Pilgrimage from Seattle to the Puyallup Fairgrounds where many of the participants and their families were incarcerated during World War II and marked the first Day of Remembrance.

A movement rooted in memory, join Frank Abe as he shares the important moment it created and stories from the experience. This talk will be paired with an art-making activity for families to honor these histories created within Seattle and we will highlight the installed Densho (Out of Many, One Display) poster at the library.

event.name: Connecting Through Culture Community Art Market
event.summary: Join SISC for our Community Art Market - Connecting Through Culture on August 22, 2026, from 11 am to 4 pm.
event.description:
The art market will be held at the future site of the Native Village & Gateway project. This event is free and open to the public! The market is a chance to check out a new set of murals that celebrate our cultures.
We invite Native and Indigenous artists and vendors, along with vendors from the Little Saigon neighborhood, to participate. The cost per vendor is $25 and we have space for 15 vendors, the deadline to apply to vend is August 7, 2026. To apply to vend, go to our website and look at our blog under 'services'.

event.name: The Man of the House Live Reading
event.description: Come to a live reading of Annie Williams's play 'The Man of the House' at Freehold's Black Box Theatre. Join us on August 27th to see 'The Man of the House,' by Annie Williams. 'The Man of the House' centers on an African American family living in Seattle in 1992, Mother (Laura), her son (Jason), & Mother’s determination to save her son from the dangers of the street. This story explores the family’s reactions to social and economic challenges facing the young man in this context of inequity. Donations are appreciated.

event.summary: Celebrate Summer with the CID Food Walk on August 29 from 11AM-4PM!
event.description:
Calling all foodies! Come try new foods and support local at the CID Food Walk. Participating businesses across Chinatown-International District will offer special $6 + $8 bites and other discounts. Food Walk is a great way to stuff your bellies and support various neighborhood businesses.

event.name: Coffee & Conversations
event.summary: Join us for a snack, some coffee or tea, and to chat with your neighbors!
event.description:
Coffee & Conversations is a space for relaxing and getting to know your neighbors! Chat about books, hobbies, the weather, or anything else on your mind.

There will be light snacks and coffee/tea provided, a place to charge your devices, books & magazines to look at, and conversation to be had.

This program was designed for insecurely-housed community members, and is free and open to all. The Library celebrates and reflects the voices, experiences and perspectives of Seattle’s diverse communities in our spaces, collections and programs. Learn more about the Library’s equity efforts at www.spl.org/Equity.

event.name: CID Night Market
event.summary: As the sun sets over the historic Chinatown Gate, experience a vibrant side of the neighborhood with an unique open-air market and live music to dance to all night.
event.description: Since 2006, the CID Night Market has provided locals and visitors a unique open-air market experience - at night. Visitors can expect to find dozens of local street vendors offering food, arts and crafts, and more. Cultural performances including a lion dance, taiko, and martial arts demonstrations will take place under the red arch in Hing Hay Park as the sun sets.
